title: SPA fallback condition is always-true, making the final 404 branch unreachable
detail: api/routes.ts trailing 404 guards on `!startsWith('/api/')` but /api/ returns earlier (line 39-41), so `!pathname.startsWith("/api/")` is always true at the catch-all (line 67) and the `return new Response("Not found", {status:404})` (line 71) is unreachable dead code. This is a correctness/quality cleanup, NOT an exploitable security issue. Re-reported 12 runs, never fixed. This run (2026-06-20T07-55) re-confirmed and clarified: simplify the guard to a bare final `return serveFile(index.html)` with the 404 dropped.

title: Path-prefix containment checks omit the trailing separator (path traversal)
detail: `startsWith(resolvedDir)` must append `path.sep` or siblings like `outputs-evil` bypass it. Recurs across gallery/caption/upload/config variants over 7 runs. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-flagged it at critical severity in api/config.ts validatePythonPath: `resolved.startsWith(REPO_DIR)` (no trailing sep, so `<REPO_DIR>-evil`/`<REPO_DIR>-extra` siblings match) COMBINED with `resolved.includes('/.venv/')` substring (any path containing that string passes). A sibling-repo binary like `<REPO_DIR>-evil/.venv/bin/python` satisfies BOTH checks, then handleVerifyPython Bun.spawnSync([bin,'-c','import mlx...']) executes it — RCE from a client-controlled config value.

title: handleVerifyPython forwards raw err.message / Python stderr to the client
detail: api/config.ts returns the spawn exception message AND the last stderr line to the client (path/env disclosure). Both paths need fixing: catch block returns e.message; non-zero exit path exposes Python traceback last line. Log server-side, return generic. Re-flagged 13 runs.

title: handleKnowledgeAnalyze exposes internal error message (may include API-key detail)
detail: api/knowledge.ts forwards err.message from DeepSeek/third-party calls to the client. Return generic error, log full detail server-side. Re-flagged 8 runs.

title: killJob lacks a pid guard and finalizes before stream drain (both the immediate-sync path AND the 5s SIGTERM fallback)
detail: lib/subprocess.ts: guard `job.pid` before process.kill(); rely on proc.exited to finalize after streams drain rather than calling finalize() directly from killJob. The spawn path (lines 230-241) deliberately awaits Promise.all([stdoutDone, stderrDone]) before finalize so trailing log lines and Saved:/Manifest: markers persist. killJob's 5s SIGTERM fallback (lines 270-282) calls finalize('failed',-1) SYNCHRONOUS inside setTimeout WITHOUT awaiting the stream drains; once finalized=true, the proc.exited->drain->finalize path is a no-op, so a run.py child that takes the SIGTERM but flushes final output between 5s and actual exit drops those lines and any final 'Saved:' output paths. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-confirmed the 5s fallback reintroduces exactly the drain-before-finalize bug the comment at 262-269 warns about. Re-flagged 7 runs.

title: isPathAllowed() defaults to full REPO_DIR instead of narrow output dirs
detail: caption/upload/caption-GET accept arbitrary client paths but allow-scope is REPO_DIR, not OUTPUT_DIRS. Narrow to the minimum dir set (OUTPUT_DIRS + UPLOAD_DIR). The trailing-separator fix is already in place (line 38 uses d + path.sep), but the SCOPE is still the full repo. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-flagged api/caption.ts handleCaptionGet: it checks only isPathAllowed(imagePath) with the default allowedDirs=[...OUTPUT_DIRS, REPO_DIR], so a client can read ANY <anything>.caption.json under the entire repository; unlike handleCaptionRun, the GET path has no leading-dash guard and no output-dir containment. Re-flagged 7 runs.

title: clearJobs accepts arbitrary status without an allowlist (HTTP handler AND low-level manager)
detail: api/jobs.ts handleClearJobs casts `status` unchecked AND lib/subprocess.ts clearJobs(statuses) deletes matching jobs without restricting to CLEARABLE=['completed','failed']. Only the HTTP handler enforces the allowlist; any future internal caller (admin route, workflow script) invoking subprocessManager.clearJobs directly could pass ['running'] and silently kill+purge in-flight jobs (deleteJob also SIGTERMs running children). Validation must live at the trust boundary (the manager), not just the route. Clamp statuses inside clearJobs itself: filter to CLEARABLE before iterating. Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: HTML shell and API responses ship without baseline security headers
detail: api/routes.ts serves HTML/health without X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff etc. Add headers on shell + API responses. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-flagged at info: handleGalleryImage DOES set nosniff on served media (gallery.ts:244,259 — verified, so stored-XSS-via-sniff is closed), and all JSON/text responses set an explicit Content-Type so the browser honors the declared type in practice; the gap is belt-and-suspenders on generic JSON error responses and the SPA shell. Re-flagged 5 runs.

title: React custom hook (useFieldHistory) called inside .map() — Rules of Hooks violation
detail: frontend/components/CommandForm.tsx calls a hook per list item, breaking hook-ordering guarantees. Hoist the hook out of the loop. Re-flagged 2 runs.

title: Gallery DELETE trusts client-supplied dirIdx/name without verifying the entry was listed
detail: api/gallery.ts: path-prefix containment is not membership verification. Re-check dirIdx/name against a server-side scan before deleting. Re-flagged 2 runs.

title: FTS5 'optimize' runs after _indexed=true, so a thrown optimize masks build failure
detail: lib/gallery-index.ts buildIndex sets `_indexed = true` (line 50) BEFORE running `INSERT INTO images_fts(images_fts) VALUES('optimize')` (line 51). If optimize throws (corrupt/large FTS5 index, OOM), the exception propagates but isIndexed() already returns true, so handleGallerySearch never retries the build — subsequent searches run against a half-built/under-optimized index and return empty/wrong results with no rebuild triggered. Wrap DELETE+insertAll+optimize in try/catch; set _indexed=true ONLY after full success, reset to false on failure. Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: handlePutConfig accepts arbitrary outputDir/modelsDir without path-containment validation
detail: api/config.ts write-time path is not bounded — a client can point generation at any directory. Validate against an allowlist at write time; reject absolute paths or traversal (..) that escape the allowed root. At minimum require they resolve within REPO_DIR or its sibling output store. Re-flagged 2 runs. Retired: subsumed under path-prefix-missing-separator + validate-python-path-substring-not-prefix which cover the same config.ts write-path class at higher signal.

title: CSRF/origin check compares against the request's own Host header (DNS-rebinding bypass)
detail: api/routes.ts (line 94) and api/ws.ts (line 23): origin allowlist is derived from Host header — DNS-rebinding makes attacker origin match. Because no POST endpoint has other auth, a matching origin lets a malicious page POST /api/run, /api/upload, /api/config (combined with validatePythonPath = RCE), /api/gallery DELETE. Use a fixed allowlist: `new Set(['http://localhost:3099', 'http://127.0.0.1:3099'])`. Mirror in both HTTP routes and WS upgrade. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-flagged the same allowlist construction duplicated verbatim in routes.ts:95-116 and ws.ts:23-40 — the Host-derived port extraction + [127.0.0.1,localhost,[::1]] list is copy-pasted, and the default port '3099' is hardcoded as a string fallback in both (plus server.ts:15 numeric). Re-flagged 6 runs.

title: Upload/gallery serves files without Content-Type + nosniff (stored XSS via polyglot/SVG/HTML)
detail: api/gallery.ts + api/upload.ts: extension-only upload check + missing nosniff lets a polyglot payload execute. Sniff content and set headers. Retired: single-occurrence; the header/nosniff gap is already covered by missing-security-headers which recurs 5x at higher confidence.

title: Upload file-size check runs after the full multipart body is parsed into memory
detail: api/upload.ts: check Content-Length before req.formData() to fail-fast; post-parse check must remain as backstop (Content-Length can be spoofed). This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-confirmed: handleUpload calls `await req.formData()` (line 38) BEFORE the size guard (line 64). server.ts sets maxRequestBodySize:50MB (line 28) as the real framing-layer backstop, so the per-file 50MB check is redundant in practice — the finding stands as fail-fast hygiene, not an exploitable overrun. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: File-path string fields passed to the subprocess skip path-containment checks
detail: lib/args.ts forwards path fields to run.py without containment; apply the same boundary as the API layer. (Distinct from the startsWith-separator bug.) Retired to compact active records to <=40: single-occurrence (1x, conf 0.8), the lowest-confidence/lowest-occurrence active record; the path-containment class is well-covered by path-prefix-missing-separator (7x) and validate-python-path-substring-not-prefix (5x).

title: Persistent hotspots: api/routes.ts, api/gallery.ts, lib/knowledge-extractor.ts, api/models.ts, api/knowledge.ts, api/model-check.ts, lib/code-knowledge.ts, lib/knowledge-db.ts, frontend/hooks/ui/wsClient.ts
detail: Across 16 runs these files attract the most findings. This run (2026-06-20T04-15, full-scope 191 files / 15596 lines): api/routes.ts=3 (170-line if/else chain + duplicated CORS allowlist + hardcoded port), api/gallery.ts=2, lib/knowledge-extractor.ts=2, api/models.ts=3 (lorals typo + dead req param + hand-copied manifest fields), lib/paths.ts=2, lib/code-knowledge.ts=1 (hardcoded user path — FIXED this run), lib/knowledge-db.ts=1 (hardcoded user path — FIXED this run), frontend/hooks/ui/wsClient.ts=1 (reconnect-timer-not-cleared ported to singleton). code-quality dimension dominated (17 of 26) this run. The recurring security/correctness classes persist on api/config.ts/api/model-check.ts/lib/subprocess.ts (not re-flagged this run but unfixed).

title: Fix mode is now exercised: this run applied 2 verified fixes (first non-review-only run) — recurring findings can now be closed
detail: Prior 15 runs were review-only (effort:low, fixes.applied=0). This run (2026-06-20T04-15) was effort:medium + fix:true: 26 findings, adversarial verdicts=2 upheld=2 (rejection_rate=0, reversing the prior 0.75 trend), fixes.applied=2 (code-knowledge.ts + knowledge-db.ts hardcoded user paths → REPO_DIR-derived), regressions=0, testBaseline 546 pass / 0 fail = testPostFix 546/0, tscDelta=0, treeDirty=false. Lesson: fix:true with a clean tree is safe here (no regressions); the two highest-confidence hardcoded-path findings were closed in one pass. Supersedes the prior low-effort-review-only-no-fix record.

title: Prior 15 runs were review-only (effort:low) — zero fixes applied
detail: Historical record: all 15 runs before 2026-06-20T04-15 were review-only with fixes.applied=0, so recurring findings stayed unfixed. Superseded by fix-mode-baseline-shifted: the 2026-06-20T04-15 run was the first effort:medium+fix:true run and applied 2 verified fixes with no regressions. Retained for history.

title: Findings skew to security + correctness historically, but code-quality is the dominant volume in full-scope scans
detail: This run (2026-06-20T04-15, full-scope): code-quality=17 of 26 findings (the bulk — duplication/hardcoded-paths/typo/dead-param/refactor opportunities), correctness=4, security=4, error-handling=1. CORRECTION to prior framing: the 'sparse code-quality' claim was an artifact of incremental (changed-files-only) scans; a full-scope scan surfaces a large code-quality tail. Security+correctness remain the HIGH-severity concentration (this run: 2 high both code-quality hardcoded-path, 6 medium, 16 low, 2 info). The security/correctness findings are the ones that warrant fix:true; code-quality is mostly refactor-nit volume.

title: Top recurring findings are real defects (FP-rate 0); adversarial rejection rate is RUN-DEPENDENT not monotonic
detail: Reflection: correctness/security avg_fp_rate across prior runs is 0 — recurring findings (SPA-404, path-traversal, error-leak, CSRF-rebinding, validate-python-path) are real, unfixed defects. NOTE the rejection-rate signal is NOISY not trending: 2026-06-20T03-24 had adversarial_rejection_rate=0.75 (3 of 4 rejected), 2026-06-20T04-15 had rejection_rate=0 (2 of 2 upheld), and 2026-06-20T06-08 had rejection_rate=1.0 (1 of 1 rejected — the lone finding from a 2-file incremental scan was adversarially rejected, zero persisted). The three samples swing 0.0 → 0.75 → 1.0 across consecutive runs. Do NOT read a trend from a 1/2/4-verdict sample — the re-report-the-recurrence rule holds for long-lived findings; per-finding close inspection (pattern-usage-aware-flagging) remains necessary but is not validated by the small adversarial sample. The 06-08 run also confirms a small-scope incremental scan (2 files / 412 lines) commonly yields only a single low-value finding that the adversarial gate rejects (see small-scope-incremental-near-zero-yield).

title: job_failed WS message received but frontend never calls setOutputFiles for it
detail: frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts: job_complete handler calls setOutputFiles but job_failed does not. The WS broadcast in api/ws.ts sends outputFiles for BOTH completed and failed jobs, so a job that fails mid-run carries already-produced outputs that the frontend silently discards. Fix: add `if (msg.outputFiles?.length) setOutputFiles(msg.outputFiles)` in the job_failed branch. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: useCommandView substitutes WS logs over restored job logs even when job is not running
detail: frontend/hooks/commands/useCommandView.ts derivedJob uses WS `logs` when `logs.length > 0`, regardless of job.status. A restored completed/failed job can show stale WS logs from a prior subscription until subscribe() fires. Fix: gate the WS log substitution on `job.status === 'running' && logs.length > 0`. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: WebSocket reconnect timer not cleared before setting new timer on close (double-reconnect) — bug recurs in the SHARED wsClient singleton after the useWebSocket fix
detail: The fix landed in frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts:55 (`if (reconnectTimer.current) clearTimeout(reconnectTimer.current)`) but was NEVER PORTED to the shared broadcast singleton frontend/hooks/ui/wsClient.ts. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-flagged wsClient.ts:27 — ws.onclose assigns `_reconnectTimer = window.setTimeout(_connect, _reconnectDelay)` without first clearing a pending timer. If onclose fires twice in quick succession (ws.close() from onerror racing a transport close) the first handle is orphaned and both fire _connect. The singleton drives ALL broadcast listeners (useJobs revalidation, gallery-updated, hmr-reload), so a leaked timer storm degrades the whole SPA. Fix (same as the useWebSocket fix): `if (_reconnectTimer) clearTimeout(_reconnectTimer)` before the setTimeout. LESSON: a correctness fix applied to one site of a duplicated pattern must be grep-ported to every sibling site, or the bug class recurs. Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: Gallery DELETE companion-file cleanup uses only the verbatim base name, missing multi-segment suffixes (read/write asymmetry)
detail: api/gallery.ts handleGalleryDelete deletes `{base}.manifest.json` etc., but for relay/segment filenames like `output_20260611_193630_seg01.png` the real manifest is the parent stem `output_20260611_193630.manifest.json` (found by findCompanionJson via progressive suffix-stripping). The delete handler never strips these suffixes so orphaned .manifest.json/.run.json/.caption.json remain across output dirs. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-confirmed the exact asymmetry: READ path resolves companions by progressively stripping `_relay`/`_segXX`; DELETE path only strips the file extension. Fix: reuse findCompanionJson(dir, base, suffix) per companion type, then tryDelete the resolved path (export it; keeps delete symmetric with list). Re-flagged 4 runs.

title: validatePythonPath uses substring match for /.venv/ allowing arbitrary paths that contain the string
detail: api/config.ts `resolved.includes('/.venv/')` passes `/tmp/evil/.venv/bin/python` and `resolved.includes('/venv/')` passes `/home/attacker/venv/bin/malicious`. The malicious binary is then invoked by handleVerifyPython (Bun.spawnSync) and by caption/model-check via resolvePythonBin — an arbitrary-command-execution primitive via the config write endpoint. This run (2026-06-19T22:47) re-flagged it as severity:critical (the highest-severity finding). A sibling-repo binary like `<REPO_DIR>-evil/.venv/bin/python` passes BOTH the startsWith(REPO_DIR) check (prefix, no trailing sep) AND the includes('/.venv/') check. Since a config PUT writes it to disk, every subsequent run.py/check-model/caption spawn runs arbitrary code as the server user. Fix: drop the includes() branches entirely; use strict directory containment with a trailing separator — `if (!resolved.startsWith(REPO_DIR + path.sep)) return false;`. If an out-of-repo venv must be supported, validate against an explicit allowlist of resolved venv roots. Re-flagged 5 runs.

title: callDeepSeek makes outbound fetch without an AbortSignal timeout (indefinite hang, request-slot exhaustion)
detail: lib/knowledge-extractor.ts callDeepSeek: no AbortSignal on the fetch to api.deepseek.com. A slow/stalled response holds the server request open indefinitely, exhausting request slots on the single Bun event loop. The function is awaited end-to-end through the HTTP handler so the client connection also hangs. Compare with vlm.ts which uses AbortSignal.timeout(5000). Fix: add `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)`, catch TimeoutError in handleKnowledgeAnalyze's existing try/catch. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: Caption API forwards style/prompt to subprocess without allowlist or length cap
detail: api/caption.ts handleCaptionRun: `style` passed to run.py without enum check (valid: default/photography/t2i/profile/style/score/compare/review/playwright), and `prompt` has no length cap. Large prompts (up to 50MB body limit) forwarded verbatim to the VLM subprocess — DoS. style/prompt follow value-taking flags so argparse won't misparse as flags, but the lack of an allowlist/length cap is still an input-validation gap. The `image` positional is already guarded against leading-dash injection. Fix: allowlist style; cap prompt at ~4000 chars before spawning. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: handleModelCheck returns raw run.py stderr to client; handleModelCheckCache is the one inconsistent handler forwarding e.message
detail: api/model-check.ts: on non-JSON output the raw decoded stderr is returned directly as the `error` field, and on a spawn exception the raw e.message is returned. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) isolated the inconsistency: every error path in this file EXCEPT handleModelCheckCache (line 67) was hardened to log server-side + return generic; handleModelCheckCache still returns `"Failed to read cache: " + (e.message || String(e))` — the one inconsistent handler, embedding filesystem paths/SQLite internals in the response. Same info-disclosure class as verify-python-leaks-stderr. Fix: align handleModelCheckCache with the others — console.error + return generic. Re-flagged 5 runs.

title: proc.stdout/stderr.getReader() runs outside the try/catch, leaving job stuck 'running'
detail: lib/subprocess.ts: proc.stdout/stderr are null-checked (line 143) inside the try/catch, but `proc.stdout.getReader()` / `proc.stderr.getReader()` on lines 210-211 run OUTSIDE that try/catch (which ends at line 133). If getReader() throws synchronously (a stream in an errored state), the exception propagates out of spawn(): finalize is never registered, the job stays status 'running' forever, the request handler crashes, and the orphaned job can never be finalized or cleanly killed. Fix: wrap the getReader() calls in the same finalize-as-failed guard used for the null-stream case (push stderr log, set status=failed, exitCode=-1, broadcastStatus, return id). Retired: single-occurrence latent trap in the subprocess class; killjob-pid-guard-and-finalize (7x, conf 0.9) is the higher-signal recurring record for this file.

title: handleListLoras/handleListVaes expose absolute filesystem paths to unauthenticated clients
detail: api/models.ts: both model-listing endpoints return `path` as an absolute filesystem path (e.g. /Users/<user>/proj/.../python/mlx-movie-director/models/lora/<name>) for every LoRA/VAE entry. The frontend only needs the model name and relative identifiers (it builds CLI args via buildCliArgs which itself resolves and validates against allowed dirs). Leaking the full absolute path reveals the OS username and directory layout of the host. Combined with the lack of auth on the API, this is an unnecessary info-disclosure vector. Fix: return the model name/relative subfolder (e.g. path: entry.name) instead of the absolute path. Re-flagged 2 runs.

title: Before FLAGGING info-disclosure/error-handling/security issues, grep call-site usage + scan ~70 lines for an existing guard
detail: Mitigates the high false-positive rate at flag-time. For each candidate: (1) grep the repo for callers/readers of the flagged symbol or endpoint; (2) scan ~70 lines around the site and the auth middleware for an existing guard or benign context (localhost dev tool, functional identity, upstream try/catch). If a guard exists or the context is benign, downgrade severity or drop the finding instead of emitting a context-free pattern match. Do NOT rely on the adversarial-verify gate to filter these — it reports upheld=0 yet leaves findings verified (sample sizes are tiny: this run 2/2 upheld, prior run 1/4 upheld — the gate is too small-sample to be a reliable filter). CALIBRATION UPDATE (2026-06-20T04-15): this run's full-scope scan produced 26 high-confidence findings with rejection_rate=0, so the close-inspection burden is lower when the finding set is already high-confidence; apply the grep+guard check most aggressively to info-disclosure/security-severity candidates where the localhost single-operator threat model downgrades real impact.

title: handleGetLastJob returns null when command filter is absent instead of the actual last job
detail: api/jobs.ts: the ternary's else branch is `null`, so GET /api/jobs/last without a command returns `{ job: null }` even when jobs exist. The route name implies 'most recent job regardless of command'. Latent (frontend always passes command) but any caller omitting it silently gets nothing. Fix: fall back to `jobs.find(j => j.status !== 'running') ?? null` when command is absent. Retired: single-occurrence latent trap; no caller omits command, so the dead branch never fires in practice.

title: handleGalleryImage serves any file under OUTPUT_DIRS by normalized path with no realpath or extension allowlist
detail: api/gallery.ts: containment uses path.normalize+startsWith (lexical only — no realpath), so a symlink under an output dir whose target is outside passes the check while Bun.file follows the link. No MEDIA_GLOB extension allowlist either (unlike handleGalleryDelete), so manifest.json/run.json/caption.json or attacker-placed files are servable. octet-stream+nosniff backstop prevents active execution, but sensitive companion JSON or symlinked files are readable by any local requester. Fix (two-layer): realpathSync before prefix check; gate name on MEDIA_GLOB.match like the delete path does. This run (2026-06-20T04-15) re-confirmed at info severity: the trailing-sep prefix check is CORRECT (resolvedDir = path.resolve(dir)+path.sep), the gap is purely the missing realpath — and the only actor who can plant a symlink under OUTPUT_DIRS is the operator (who already has a shell), so not exploitable by the threat model, but worth noting for defense-in-depth. Re-flagged 3 runs.

title: loadJobs crashes server boot if any persisted job has missing/non-array logs or outputUrls
detail: lib/jobstore.ts loadJobs iterates loaded jobs and reads `job.logs.length` unconditionally, then loadAndRestoreJob pushes to job.logs. If jobs.json contains a job whose `logs` (or `outputUrls`) field is undefined/null — hand-edited, partial write, older/malformed schema, or a job persisted before the LogLine migration — `job.logs.length` throws TypeError and, because loadAndRestoreJobs runs at server.ts startup, the ENTIRE server fails to boot. No defensive coercion is applied. Fix: coerce before access — `if (!Array.isArray(job.logs)) job.logs = []; if (!Array.isArray(job.outputUrls)) job.outputUrls = [];` and `if (!job.startedAt) continue;` to skip wholly malformed entries rather than crashing the migration loop.

title: saveJobs is fire-and-forget Bun.write with no serialization — concurrent overwrites lose jobs (last-completion-wins)
detail: lib/jobstore.ts saveJobs calls Bun.write(...) unawaited (.catch(()=>{})). broadcastStatus() triggers persistJobs→saveJobs on EVERY log line AND every status change. Two rapid broadcasts each snapshot and write asynchronously; the OS may complete the OLDER write after the NEWER one, clobbering newest state with a stale snapshot (last-write-wins by completion order, not issue order). On a busy job emitting many log lines this silently drops the completed/failed transition or resurrects a 'running' state from a stale write landing last. Fix: serialize with a promise chain capturing the snapshot synchronously — `let _chain = Promise.resolve(); export function saveJobs(jobs){ const snap=[...jobs]; _chain = _chain.then(()=>Bun.write(JOBS_PATH, JSON.stringify(snap,null,2)+"\n")).catch(()=>{}); return _chain; }`.

title: JobHistoryView auto-expand-most-recent-failed useState initializer runs before SWR resolves (feature is dead)
detail: frontend/views/jobs/JobHistoryView.tsx: useState(() => {...}) initializer captures `jobs` from useJobs() at first render. On first render SWR has not resolved so jobs===[], and `sorted.find(j=>j.status==='failed')` returns undefined → expandedId stays null FOREVER (the initializer never re-runs). The intended 'auto-expand the most recent failed job' UX only works if jobs are already in cache on mount; after a fresh load the feature is dead. Fix: track a loaded-once flag and expand on the transition via useEffect — `const [autoExpanded, setAutoExpanded] = useState(false); useEffect(()=>{ if(!autoExpanded && jobs.some(j=>j.status==='failed')){ const f=[...jobs].sort((a,b)=>new Date(b.startedAt)-new Date(a.startedAt)).find(j=>j.status==='failed'); if(f){ setExpandedId(f.id); setAutoExpanded(true);} } }, [jobs, autoExpanded]);`.

title: handleGallerySearch builds the FTS index with no concurrency guard — duplicate concurrent rebuilds + invalidate race
detail: api/gallery.ts handleGallerySearch: two concurrent /api/gallery/search calls both observe isIndexed()===false and each invoke buildIndex(scanAllImages()) (a filesystem scan + INSERT loop). buildIndex does `DELETE FROM images_fts` then re-inserts — if call B's DELETE lands between call A's DELETE and A's INSERTs, call A inserts into an empty table then B deletes them again, so the index ends empty/inconsistent while both think it is built. invalidateIndex() (fired on job_complete / file watcher) can flip _indexed=false mid-build too. No mutex serializes the single-writer rebuild. Fix: guard with a module-level in-flight promise — `let _buildPromise = null; export async function ensureIndex(){ if(isIndexed()) return; if(!_buildPromise) _buildPromise = (async()=>{ buildIndex(scanAllImages()); })(); await _buildPromise; _buildPromise=null; }` and have search await ensureIndex() before querying. Sibling of fts5-optimize-masks-build-failure (that is flag-ordering; this is the concurrency-guard gap). Retired: single-occurrence low-confidence; sibling fts5-optimize-masks-build-failure (4x, conf 0.9) is the higher-signal record for the gallery-index file.

title: handleRunJob response leaks the spawned child PID to the client
detail: lib/requestUtils.ts spawnJobResponse returns `{ jobId, status, pid: job?.pid }` to the client. The child PID is process-internal info with no UI use; on an unauthenticated localhost server it aids an attacker in correlating/locating spawned run.py processes (and, with the unguarded process.kill paths in subprocess.ts, is a small step toward process-management abuse). Low impact but unnecessary disclosure. Fix: omit pid from the client-facing response — `return Response.json({ jobId, status: job?.status });` — keep pid internal to the Job object for killJob/deleteJob use. Retired: single-occurrence low-impact info-disclosure on a localhost single-operator server.

title: ImagePreview prev/next callbacks recompute findIndex per render and can desync from the button disabled-state
detail: frontend/views/gallery/GalleryView.tsx: the onPrev/onNext/hasPrev/hasNext props each call allImages.findIndex(previewImage.url) inline during render (4 linear scans per render). These are inline closures recreated every render and previewImage can change between render and click; hasPrev/hasNext computed at render time can disagree with the click handler's findIndex if allImages mutated (e.g. a delete) in between — e.g. hasNext says true but onNext's findIndex now returns the last index and does nothing. Minor correctness/UX glitch; the keyboard effect (lines 50-69) uses a single consistent idx so keyboard nav is fine, but the on-screen prev/next buttons can silently no-op. Fix: compute idx once per render and reuse. Retired: single-occurrence minor UX nit, no recurrence across 16 runs.

title: useDefaultState lists serverDefaults object identity in deps, re-merging unnecessarily
detail: frontend/hooks/useDefaultState.ts: an object identity in a useEffect dep array triggers re-merge on every render. Depend on primitive fields instead. Retired: single-occurrence low-severity code-quality nit, superseded by higher-signal correctness/security patterns.

title: useLoras clears _fetching before setting _cache on the success path (cache race)
detail: frontend/hooks/useLoras.ts: ordering lets concurrent callers re-fetch. Set the cache before clearing the fetching flag. Retired: single-occurrence, subsumed under the broader frontend-race/recurrence patterns.

title: Cross-module singletons (subprocessManager) used without a matching import
detail: Handlers use a process/global singleton but omit its import (api/selftest.ts used subprocessManager unimported — runtime NameError). Grep usage vs imports. Retired: one-off bug already fixed; no recurrence in 13 runs.

title: Bun.serve request.json() returns unknown — destructured without validation
detail: Handlers destructure body.dirIdx/body.name directly from `unknown`. Validate/cast before field access to avoid runtime type errors. Retired: single-occurrence type-safety nit; the type-safety dimension continues near-zero yield (see dimension-calibration-skewed).

title: subprocess readStream drops partial lines spanning chunk boundaries
detail: lib/subprocess.ts readStream must carry a `pending` buffer across read() chunks and flush on close, else log lines split across reads vanish. Retired: single-occurrence; overlapped with subprocess-getreader-outside-try and killjob-pid-guard-and-finalize which cover the same file with higher signal.

title: useWebSocket progress regex matches incidental percentages in non-progress log lines (memory: 80%, loaded 50% of weights)
detail: frontend/hooks/ui/useWebSocket.ts line 72: `const pm = msg.line.match(/\b(\d{1,3})%/) ?? msg.line.match(/step (\d+) of (\d+)/i);`. The percent matcher `\b(\d{1,3})%` is unanchored to any progress context, so a stray number followed by '%' that is NOT actual progress (e.g. 'memory: 80%' from a system metric, or 'loaded 50% of weights at step 3 of 10' which matches 50% and ignores the more meaningful step ratio) incorrectly sets the progress bar. When the percent branch matches, pm[2] is undefined so the pct branch correctly uses +pm[1], but the SOURCE is wrong. The clamp (0..100) only bounds the value, not the relevance. Fix: restrict the percent match to an explicit progress context, e.g. `/progress[:\s]+(\d{1,3})%/i` or `/\b(\d{1,3})%\s*(?:complete|done)?/i`, and drop the bare `\b(\d{1,3})%` catch-all. Retired: single-occurrence minor UX nit (progress bar momentarily shows a wrong value); cosmetic, no recurrence.

title: knowledge-extractor formatRecord interpolates run.steps/cfg_scale/width/height/lora_scale without null guards — malformed run.json injects 'undefined' tokens into the DeepSeek prompt
detail: lib/knowledge-extractor.ts formatRecord builds the pipeline line via template literals: `Steps: ${run.steps} | CFG: ${run.cfg_scale} | Size: ${run.width}x${run.height}`. The run object is guaranteed truthy by the eligible filter (requires r.run) but its SCALAR fields are NOT validated. A run.json missing steps/cfg_scale/width/height/lora_scale produces literal 'undefined' / 'undefinedxundefined' tokens in the prompt sent to DeepSeek, corrupting knowledge extraction with garbage values. run.lora_scale is also accessed directly and is undefined when no LoRA is used, producing 'none @ undefined'. Fix: default the scalars before interpolating — `const steps = run.steps ?? "?"; const cfg = run.cfg_scale ?? "?"; const size = run.width && run.height ? \`${run.width}x${run.height}\` : "?"; const loraScale = run.lora_scale ?? "none";` — so malformed run.json degrades gracefully instead of injecting 'undefined'. Re-confirmed this run (2026-06-20T04-15) at the same locus (formatRecord). Re-flagged 2 runs.

title: Gallery scan filter only excludes _relay.png — relay thumbnails with other extensions (.jpg/.webp thumb) leak as top-level gallery entries
detail: api/gallery.ts line 85 filters media scan results with `.filter((f) => !f.endsWith("_relay.png"))`. But video relay/thumbnail companions for .mp4/.mov/.webm segments, or any `_relay`-suffixed file with a different extension, are NOT excluded. The companion-lookup logic at line 118 only looks for `.png` thumbnails (`${base}_relay.png` and `${base}.png`), so a stray `_relay.jpg` or `_relay.webp` is surfaced as its own top-level gallery entry rather than treated as a thumbnail for its parent video. This pollutes the gallery grid with thumbnail images that have no manifest/run companion. Fix: broaden the exclusion to all relay thumbnails regardless of extension — `.filter((f) => !/_relay\.[^.]+$/.test(f))`, or exclude any file whose stem ends with `_relay`. Retired: single-occurrence minor scan-filter nit; the gallery class is already covered by gallery-delete-misses-multi-segment-companions (4x) and gallery-image-no-symlink-resolution (3x).

title: Scan flags code that is correct on close inspection: (a) loadJobs legacy-log migration is sound; (b) caption stdout-drain ordering avoids the documented deadlock
detail: Two findings self-rejected on inspection: (1) correctness-jobstore.ts-39 — the loadJobs migration at line 39 wraps legacy string logs as {text,stream} correctly; the line 37 guard sets job.logs=[] only when NOT an array, and line 38 checks length>0 && typeof[0]==='string' before mapping — NO BUG. (2) correctness-caption.ts-86 — caption drains stdout/stderr by starting new Response(stream).text() promises BEFORE awaiting proc.exited, then collecting results after; the ordering correctly avoids the documented pipe deadlock, and the error-path skip of await stdoutP is acceptable. Lesson: the scan increasingly emits 'verified, not a bug' findings; always read the surrounding guard logic (length/type checks, promise-start-before-await ordering) before treating these as actionable. Reinforces pattern-usage-aware-flagging.

title: useJobs (and other useWebSocketEvents consumers) revalidate on a WS message type the server never broadcasts — stale list for up to the refreshInterval
detail: frontend/hooks/queries/useJobs.ts: the useWebSocketEvents callback calls mutate() on `msg.type === "job_complete" || "job_failed" || "job_start"` for an instant jobs-list refresh. But the server NEVER broadcasts `type: "job_start"` — every broadcast site (api/ws.ts onStatus emits only job_complete/job_failed/log; server.ts and api/bundle.ts emit only hmr-reload/gallery-updated/hmr-error; onLog emits only log) has no code path producing it. So when a new job is spawned via /api/run, /api/replay, /api/selftest, or /api/model-check/scan, the jobs list does NOT refresh immediately — it updates only on the next refreshInterval tick (5s) or the eventual complete/failed. The History view (and any useJobs consumer) shows stale data for up to 5s after starting a job. Symptom is limited to the just-started window (complete/failed are emitted), hence medium not high. Two fix paths: (a) emit a distinct start signal — add `this.broadcastStatus(job)` in lib/subprocess.ts spawn() after `this.jobs.set(id, job)` and have ws.ts onStatus emit `{ type: "job_status", job }` for running too, with useJobs revalidating on it; or (b) simpler frontend-only fix — also refresh on the shared `log` message when a brand-new jobId appears. Class lesson: WS-revalidate hooks must only listen for types the server actually emits — grep the broadcast sites (ws.ts onStatus/onLog) before adding a type to the match list.

title: Hardcoded absolute /Users/huangziyu/... path baked into source (non-portable across machines/worktrees) — FIXED this run
detail: lib/code-knowledge.ts DEFAULT_KB_CODE_ROOT (line 15) and lib/knowledge-db.ts KB_ROOT (line 10) both embedded `/Users/huangziyu/proj/video_generation/knowledge-base` as committed defaults. The code-knowledge.ts copy was env-overridable (KB_CODE_ROOT); the knowledge-db.ts copy was NOT overridable at all, so on any other machine or worktree every ensureKbDirs/appendRecordsToDb/saveReportToDb/readAllRecordsFromDb call wrote to a nonexistent path. This is the maintainability/portability hazard the MEMORY note about worktree sharing warns about. FIX APPLIED 2026-06-20T04-15 (effort:medium+fix:true): both replaced with `path.resolve(REPO_DIR, '..', 'video_generation', 'knowledge-base'[, '/code'])`, matching the existing OUTPUT_DIRS repo-relative resolution and the ../video_generation__output pattern; knowledge-db.ts also gained a KB_ROOT env override for parity. Verified the resolved path equals the old hardcoded path on this machine (no behavior change) and the dir exists; tests 546/0 unchanged, tscDelta=0. LESSON: grep for hardcoded absolute user paths before commit — they break every worktree/CI/machine except the author's; derive from REPO_DIR + a shared relative offset.

title: A correctness/security fix applied to one site of a duplicated pattern recurs at every un-fixed sibling site — grep-port after every fix
detail: When the same logic is duplicated across files (WS reconnect timers in useWebSocket.ts vs wsClient.ts; containment checks in paths.ts/caption.ts/gallery.ts; CORS allowlist in routes.ts/ws.ts; loopback-URL guard in config.ts/vlm.ts), a fix applied to ONE copy leaves the bug class live in the others, and the reviewer re-flags it run after run. Concrete instance this run (2026-06-20T04-15): the clearTimeout-before-setTimeout reconnect fix landed in useWebSocket.ts:55 but was never ported to the shared wsClient.ts singleton (ws-reconnect-timer-not-cleared), so the bug recurred in the singleton that drives ALL broadcast listeners. WORKFLOW RULE: after any fix, grep for the duplicated pattern (the changed symbol, the regex, the guard expression) and port the fix to every sibling site in the same pass; otherwise the next review run re-flags the unfixed copy. Pair this with the 'extract shared helper' refactor (containment-check-reimplemented, cross-origin-allowlist-duplication) to eliminate the duplication root cause.

title: `resolved.startsWith(d + path.sep) || resolved === d` is reimplemented inline in 4 files instead of one shared helper
detail: The same containment expression appears in lib/paths.ts:38 (isPathAllowed), api/caption.ts:54 (handleCaptionRun) and :154 (handleCaptionGet), and api/gallery.ts:220-221 (handleGalleryImage, as `resolvedDir = path.resolve(dir)+path.sep; filePath.startsWith(resolvedDir)`). The caption/gallery copies intentionally EXCLUDE REPO_DIR, so callers cannot reuse isPathAllowed — hence the copy-paste. gallery.ts additionally diverges by using path.normalize (lexical) rather than path.resolve, so symlinks are not resolved there (see gallery-image-no-symlink-resolution). This is the root cause behind BOTH the path-prefix-missing-separator recurrence (the trailing-sep detail must be hand-copied correctly each time) and the fix-not-ported-to-sibling-sites class. Fix: add to lib/paths.ts `export function isInsideDir(child, root): boolean { const r=path.resolve(root); const c=path.resolve(child); return c===r || c.startsWith(r+path.sep); }`, build isPathAllowed + isInsideOutputDirs on top of it, and replace the inline copies. Self-documenting trailing-sep correctness everywhere. Retired: single-occurrence refactor nit; its root-cause insight is already embedded in the higher-recurrence records it points at (path-prefix-missing-separator 7x, fix-not-ported-to-sibling-sites 1x-high-conf, csrf-host-header-rebinding 6x). Compacted to keep active records <=40 after adding this run's new findings.

title: Cross-origin/CORS allowlist + default port '3099' duplicated verbatim in routes.ts and ws.ts (drift hazard)
detail: The Host-header port extraction + [127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]] allowlist construction is copy-pasted between api/routes.ts handleApi (lines 95-116) and api/ws.ts handleWebSocketUpgrade (lines 23-40). The literal default port '3099' is hardcoded as the string fallback in both files (plus server.ts:15 numeric default). A fix to one (e.g. tightening the bracketed-IPv6 extraction the comment admits is loose, or changing the listen port) must be remembered in both — and the listen port already lives in server.ts as a computed const. This duplicates the csrf-host-header-rebinding concern at the code-organization layer (that record is the security impact; this is the DRY root cause). Fix: extract `isSameOriginOrigin(origin, host): boolean` (and a shared DEFAULT_PORT const) into lib/requestUtils.ts, call from both sites. NOTE this run re-flagged the same duplication as 3 separate code-quality findings (routes-96, routes-104, vlm-63 loopback variant) — consolidate under one shared-helper refactor. Retired: single-occurrence refactor nit; the security impact and the DRY lesson both live in csrf-host-header-rebinding (6x) and fix-not-ported-to-sibling-sites. Compacted to keep active records <=40.

title: handleApi is a ~170-line sequential if/else chain (25+ pathname===&&method=== blocks) — replace with a route table
detail: api/routes.ts handleApi() dispatches via 25+ sequential `if (pathname === ... && method === ...)` blocks. Hard to scan, error-prone (ordering matters for the two startsWith('/api/jobs/') routes — a prefix route shadowing a literal must come after), and adding a route requires reading the whole function. routes.ts is a recurring hotspot (hotspot-files). Fix: a declarative table keyed by `${method} ${pathname}` with a small startsWith set for /api/jobs/ and /api/jobs/<id>, looped `for (const r of ROUTES) if (r.match(p,m)) return r.handler(req,url)`; the jobs/ prefix ordering becomes explicit via array position. The cross-origin allowlist at the top of the chain is covered separately by cross-origin-allowlist-duplication.

title: buildCliArgs forwards select/multiselect values to run.py without validating against field.choices (defense-in-depth gap)
detail: lib/args.ts buildCliArgs handles `select` (line 45) and `multiselect` (line 49) by trimming and pushing the raw value as `--flag value` — neither branch validates against the schema's field.choices allowlist (grep confirms no choices check in args.ts). So a POST /api/run body with an off-menu pipeline/lora value passes validateParams (required-fields only) and arrives at run.py as `--pipeline <value>`. THREAT MODEL CAVEAT: localhost single-operator, and argparse binds a leading-dash value after a value-taking flag as that flag's VALUE (not a new flag — distinct from positional argv injection), so this cannot inject a NEW flag; the realistic impact is run.py executing a model/pipeline string the GUI never intended to offer, not RCE. Still, the UI guarantees a fixed option set and the backend silently accepts anything — defense-in-depth is missing. Fix: in the select branch, when field.choices is defined (skip choicesFrom whose options are dynamic), `if (field.choices && !field.choices.some(c => c.value === value.trim())) throw new Error('Invalid value for ${key}')`; validate every multiselect item similarly. Distinct from args-subprocess-no-containment (path fields) and caption-style-no-enum-validation (caption style). Retired: single-occurrence low-confidence; localhost threat model + value-taking-flag semantics bound the impact to defense-in-depth only.

title: api/knowledge.ts module-scoped _scanCache is shared across requests; generateMissingCaptions mutates record objects in place (latent race)
detail: api/knowledge.ts: _scanCache is a module-level mutable read by handleKnowledgeCaptionMissing and handleKnowledgeAnalyze (`const records = _scanCache ?? scanOutputDirs()`). Two concurrent requests race on this shared state: handleKnowledgeCaptionMissing sets `_scanCache = null` at line 41 after caption generation while a concurrent analyze holds the same array reference, and generateMissingCaptions mutates `rec.caption`/`rec.hasCaption` IN PLACE on the shared record objects. Single-thread JS mitigates the worst races, but the in-place mutation + non-atomic cache reassignment is a latent correctness hazard: an analyze running concurrently with a caption-missing run can operate on a records array whose caption fields are mid-mutation. Fix: pass records by value (snapshot the array + shallow-copy records before the caption loop so a concurrent analyze reads a consistent view), or have generateMissingCaptions return updated copies rather than mutating shared objects. Retired: single-occurrence low-confidence latent trap; single-thread JS bounds the practical impact.

title: Small-scope incremental review runs (few changed files) commonly yield zero durable findings — the lone finding is adversarially rejected
detail: Counterweight to dimension-calibration-skewed (full-scope scans surface a large code-quality tail). An incremental review-only run with a tiny scope (2026-06-20T06-08: 2 files / 412 lines, lib layer) produced exactly ONE finding, and the adversarial gate REJECTED it (totalVerdicts=1, upheld=0, rejected=1, adversarial_rejection_rate=1.0, newFindings persisted=0). fixes.mode=review-only so nothing applied. PRACTICAL TAKEAWAY: (1) when git.headBefore shows minimal churn (1-3 lib files), the incremental scan is near-noise — do not interpret an all-rejected small-scope run as a quality regression, and do not escalate it to effort:medium+fix (nothing to fix, wasted agent time); (2) the recurring-finding signal comes from LONG-LIVED findings that re-report on the hotspot files regardless of incremental scope (see unfixed-recurrence-is-real-not-noise) — a clean incremental run does NOT mean those are resolved, only that the hotspot files were not in this run's diff; (3) to actually move health, run a full-scope scan (effort:high) periodically, not more frequent tiny incremental ones. Pair with the scan.layers breakdown: lib-only scopes have historically low durable yield vs api/frontend layers where the security/correctness findings concentrate.

title: api/models.ts LoRA accumulator misspelled as `lorals` (internally consistent, not a bug — grep-ability/readability nit)
detail: handleListLoras in api/models.ts declares `const lorals: LoraInfo[] = []` then both pushes to it (`lorals.push(...)`) and returns it (`return Response.json(lorals)`). The misspelling is internally consistent so it is NOT a functional bug, but it is a copy-paste/typo that breaks searchability: grepping for `loras` to find LoRA-related bindings misses this one, and readers stumble on the odd name. Harmless functionally; flagged low-severity code-quality only. Fix: rename the binding to `loras` (and its two usages on the push + return lines) for grep-ability and readability. Reinforces the hotspot-files observation that api/models.ts is a recurring code-quality locus (lorals typo + dead req param + hand-copied manifest fields across prior runs).

title: DNS-rebinding bypass of the origin allowlist is a FALSE POSITIVE under the browser-forbidden-header threat model — Origin/Host are attacker-unforgeable
detail: Counter-analysis to csrf-host-header-rebinding (6x active): the committed-KB 'DNS-rebinding bypass' framing is a false positive against a cross-SITE attacker. Origin and Host are browser-forbidden headers (the Fetch standard forbids JS from setting them on a request), so a malicious page at https://evil.com CANNOT produce `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — the browser stamps Origin with the embedding page's own origin, which fails the loopback [127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]] allowlist. A genuine DNS-rebinding attack sets Host/Origin to the ATTACKER's domain (the resolved IP), not to 127.0.0.1, so it too fails the allowlist. The origin-allowlist construction in routes.ts:95-116 and ws.ts:23-40 is therefore SOUND against the cross-site/cross-origin threat the framing worried about. CAVEAT: this does NOT clear csrf-host-header-rebinding entirely — the underlying concern worth keeping is the DRY-duplication + hardcoded-port drift (cross-origin-allowlist-duplication, now retired) and defense-in-depth (a fixed Set literal is cleaner than Host-derived port extraction). LESSON: when a security finding's exploit path depends on a browser-forbidden header, downgrade it — the local single-operator + browser-forbidden-Origin model makes the loopback allowlist sufficient; spend review effort on the actually-exploitable classes (validate-python-path-substring-not-prefix RCE, path-prefix-missing-separator).
